subject: botany_2
question_text: Tabulate any eight differences between C3 and C4 plants/cycles.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.25, printed question 18. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Examiner audit revision (2026-09-05): the card prints nine rows against a question that asks for any eight, so the s4_yield margin note now says so and neither s2_anatomy nor s4_yield treats the omission of one row as a mistake; the dimorphism point moved into the s2_anatomy why.

insider_note: The question says TABULATE. Draw the two columns and number the rows — an examiner marking eight differences in a paragraph will miss some, and that is entirely avoidable.

steps.label: First product and climate
steps.margin_note: Set up two columns on the first line and keep the row numbers aligned throughout.
steps.why: The names C3 and C4 come from the number of carbons in the first stable product, so that row explains where both names came from.
common_mistakes: Saying the first product of C4 is PGA. PGA is the C3 product; OAA is the C4 product.
Swapping the climates. C3 is temperate, C4 is tropical.
steps.memory_tip: Three carbons for C3, four for C4: the name IS the first product.

steps.label: Kranz anatomy and chloroplast dimorphism
steps.margin_note: Two rows, both about structure. These are the rows that explain the rest.
lines: 3. Leaves do NOT show Kranz anatomy.
steps.why: Kranz anatomy is the wreath of bundle sheath cells that keeps the two reactions of a C4 plant apart, so it is the structural reason for every other difference in the table. Chloroplast dimorphism is the row that follows from it: the mesophyll cells and the bundle sheath cells hold different chloroplasts.
common_mistakes: Giving Kranz anatomy to C3 plants. Only C4 leaves have it.
Calling Kranz anatomy a type of chloroplast. It is the leaf structure: a ring of bundle sheath cells around the vascular bundle.
steps.memory_tip: Kranz means wreath: only C4 leaves wear one.

steps.label: Photorespiration and transpiration
steps.margin_note: Two rows about what is lost. Both go the same way, which makes them easy to remember.
steps.why: Both rows are losses, and C4 plants avoid both because they concentrate carbon dioxide around RuBisCO instead of letting oxygen compete with it.
common_mistakes: Saying C4 plants photorespire more. C4 photorespiration is NOT detectable.
Reversing the transpiration row. C4 plants lose LESS water.
steps.memory_tip: C4 wastes less of everything: less carbon lost, less water lost.

steps.label: Efficiency, biomass and examples
steps.margin_note: Finish with the examples. Nine rows are given here; any eight of them answer the question.

lines.text: C4 fixes more carbon with less water lost

lines: 7. Less efficient at using atmospheric CO2.
| MORE efficient at using atmospheric CO2.
steps.why: The examples are the check on the whole table: maize and sugarcane are tropical grasses, which is exactly what rows 2 and 3 predict.
common_mistakes: Reversing the efficiency row. C4 plants use atmospheric CO2 MORE efficiently and produce more biomass.
Naming a C3 plant as C4. Maize, sugarcane and sorghum are the standard C4 three.
steps.memory_tip: Tropical grasses are the C4 plants: maize, sugarcane, sorghum.
